questions.question:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group?

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.. 13-Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic:** First number × (First number + 2) = Second number

 
• **8 - 72 → 8 × (8 + 2) = 8 × 10 = 80 ≠ 72**
 
• 11 - 143 → 11 × (11 + 2) = 11 × 13 = 143
 
• 7 - 63 → 7 × (7 + 2) = 7 × 9 = 63
 
• 9 - 99 → 9 × (9 + 2) = 9 × 11 = 99

Hence, '**8 - 72**' is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is NOT an example of a number tried with the following properties?

1. Sum of the digits of the third number is twice the sum of the digits of the first number.

2. Sum of the digits of the second number is thrice the sum of the digits of the first number.
questions.solution:
On applying these two properties on each option one by one we get,

1) (201, 702, 303)

Property 1: sum of the digits of the third number = 3 + 3 = 6 and sum of the digits of first number = 2 + 0 + 1 = 3 Here, this property is verified.

Property 2: sum of the digits of second number = 7 + 2 = 9 and sum of the digits of first number = 2 + 0 + 1 = 3 Here this property is verified.

2) (400, 660, 800)

Property 1: sum of the digits of the third number = 8 + 0 + 0 = 8 and sum of the digits of first number = 4 + 0 + 0 = 4 Here, this property is verified.

Property 2: sum of the digits of second number = 6 + 6 + 0 = 12 and sum of the digits of first number = 4 + 0 + 0 = 4 Here this property is verified.

3) (200, 600, 300)

Property 1: sum of the digits of the third number = 3 + 0 + 0 = 3 and sum of the digits of first number = 2 + 0 + 0 = 2 Here, this property is **not** verified.

Property 2: sum of the digits of second number = 6 + 0 + 0 = 6 and sum of the digits of first number = 2 + 0 + 0 = 2 Here this property is verified.

4) (111, 207, 222)

questions.solution:
The logic is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**The logic followed here is:

Option (1): 245 → It is a composite number.

Option (2): 385 → It is a composite number.

**Option (3): 59 → A Prime Number.**

Option (4): 315 → It is a composite number.

Here, Option (3) is NOT the same as the other.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

 
• The priority will always be the prime number in the exams.
 
• There are some standard rules which need to be followed while selecting the priority.
 
• **priority lists to be followed in exams according to their preferences are:**

 
• **Prime number.**
 
• **Square.**
 
• **Cube.**
 
• **Multiplication and divisions**
 
• **Addition and subtraction.**

 
• A prime number can be divided, without a remainder, only by itself and by 1.
 
• **Some facts about the Prime numbers:**

 
• The only even prime number is 2. All other even numbers can be divided by 2.
 
• If the sum of a number's digits is a multiple of 3, that number can be divided by 3.
 
• No prime number greater than 5 ends in a 5. Any number greater than 5 that ends in a 5 can be divided by 5.
 
• Zero and 1 are not considered prime numbers.
 
• Except for 0 and 1, a number is either a prime number or a composite number. A composite number is defined as any number, greater than 1, that is not prime.
